title: 02 Graphs and forms of linear equations: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 02 Graphs and forms of linear equations: Visual Guide

1. Solve Then See | lesson 01's y = mx + b as a model beside the same equation as a line, with draggable m and b, the y-intercept and x-intercept marked, and the solve-for-zero algebra printed live | an intercept is what you get by setting the other variable to zero, so the x-intercept is last lesson's one-variable equation drawn, and m = 0 gives slope zero with no x-intercept while a vertical line has no m at all

2. Rise Over Run | two draggable points with the dashed rise-and-run triangle between them, the slope computed as a reduced fraction, and the three wrong assemblies of the same four numbers evaluated alongside | slope is (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) with both differences taken in the same order, zero on top means a horizontal line of slope 0 and zero on the bottom means a vertical line whose slope is undefined

3. One Line Three Forms | slope, intercept and a chosen point driving slope-intercept, point-slope and standard form simultaneously over one unchanging graph, with step-by-step conversion in either direction and presets for the quiz equations | the three forms are encodings of one line, so converting is pure rearrangement - solve for y to reach slope-intercept dividing every term including the constant, clear fractions and force A > 0 to reach standard form

4. Name That Form | seven equations classified on tap with the facts each form hands over for free, plus a nudge slider that shifts every constant while no classification changes | form is the shape of the template and not the digits in it, so y = mx + b shows slope and y-intercept directly, point-slope shows a point and a slope, standard form shows neither, and x = a is the vertical line only standard form can write

5. Parallel Or Perpendicular | one draggable slope drawing a parallel pair with its constant gap or a perpendicular pair with a drawn right angle on equal axes, a vertical-lines mode, and the four candidate slopes sorted live | parallel means equal slopes with different intercepts, perpendicular means negative reciprocals with m1·m2 = -1, and two distinct vertical lines are always parallel although the product test cannot express it
